options_evaluated: Recycled post-consumer thermoplastic (rPCR-ABS) with molded-in structural ribbing
assessments.recommendation: Recycled post-consumer thermoplastic (rPCR-ABS) with load- and stress-optimized molded-in structural ribbing
assessments.rationale: This option directly incorporates recycled materials (h) to reduce the material footprint (o) and carbon/environmental footprint (m) of the product (Page 2, Page 33). By using load- and stress-optimisation of structures and lower density materials, it achieves lightweight design (t) goals (Page 80). Avoiding glass-fiber reinforcements ensures the housing does not contain substances of concern (f) that impair the technical properties or value of the recycled material, thereby optimizing design for recycling (d) (Page 35).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing stage (recycled plastics can exhibit higher shrinkage and lower dimensional stability, complicating the injection molding process) and Use phase (lower impact resistance compared to virgin glass-filled nylon under heavy drop tests).

options_evaluated: Threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts
assessments.recommendation: Threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts
assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners enable ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly (Page 79), which is critical for design for recycling (d) and the incorporation of used components (k) during remanufacturing (Page 33, Page 79). Avoiding structural adhesives ensures that no chemical substances of concern (f) are introduced that would make the recycling process more complicated, costly, or environmentally impactful (Page 35). This also lowers the overall material footprint (o) by facilitating component recovery.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing stage (threaded fasteners increase assembly cycle times and labor costs compared to rapid ultrasonic welding) and Use phase (vibrations during screwdriving may loosen screws over time).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets
Brushed DC motor with glued ferrite magnets
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets
assessments.rationale: Brushless motors support lightweight design (t) by optimizing power-to-weight ratio and reducing material consumption (Page 80), which minimizes the product's overall weight and volume (j). Designing the motor with non-glued, easily extractable magnets ensures that critical raw materials can be separated without non-destructive damage, supporting design for recycling (d) and avoiding contamination by adhesive substances of concern (f) (Page 35, Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Sourcing stage (neodymium magnets carry high environmental and material footprints during raw extraction, despite being highly recyclable) and Manufacturing stage (requires more complex electronic drive controllers).

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via integrated housing vents and detachable recycled aluminum heat sink
Active fan cooling integrated into the motor rotor
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via integrated housing vents and detachable recycled aluminum heat sink
assessments.rationale: Integrating thermal venting directly into the housing structure aligns with lightweight design (t) by promoting the integration of functions within a single component (Page 80). Using a detachable heat sink made from recycled aluminum supports the use of recycled materials (h) and lowers the environmental footprint (m) (Page 2, Page 33). This avoids potting compounds or PCMs which function as substances of concern (f) that complicate material recovery and recycling (d) (Page 35).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use phase (passive cooling provides lower thermal dissipation efficiency under continuous high-torque operations compared to active fan cooling, potentially reducing the tool's duty cycle).

options_evaluated: Fully modular architecture with segregated, plug-and-play functional blocks
Semi-modular architecture with soldered wire connections
assessments.recommendation: Fully modular architecture with segregated, plug-and-play functional blocks
assessments.rationale: A fully modular architecture uses standard components and material coding standards to facilitate ease of upgrading, reuse, and remanufacturing (Page 79). This design decision directly supports the incorporation of used components (k) and reduces the product's environmental footprint (m) and material footprint (o) by preventing premature waste generation (Page 2, Page 33). Coded, modular components also greatly enhance design for recycling (d) at end-of-life.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing stage (modular connectors and separate housings increase assembly complexity and initial production costs) and Sourcing stage (increases the total volume and weight (j) of the internal wiring and connector components).

options_evaluated: Removable, modular Li-ion battery pack with standardized cell housing
assessments.recommendation: Removable, modular Li-ion battery pack with standardized cell housing
assessments.rationale: Batteries contain substances of concern (f) that must be tracked and safely decontaminated at end-of-life (Page 9). A modular, removable pack ensures ease of non-destructive disassembly (Page 79) to isolate these substances, optimizing design for recycling (d) and preventing hazardous waste (Page 33, Page 35). Utilizing recycled plastics (h) for the pack casing minimizes the overall material footprint (o) (Page 2).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use phase (removable battery packs add bulk, increasing the product's weight and volume (j) compared to an integrated battery design, which may impact user ergonomics).
